title.zh: 卷一百十五 志第六十八 禮十八
title.raw: 卷一百十五 志第六十八 禮十八 Volume 115 Treatises 68: Rites 18

sentences.zh: 禮十八

translations.literal: Rites 18
translations.idiomatic: Rites 18

sentences.zh: 〈（嘉禮六）

translations.literal: (Auspicious Rites VI)
translations.idiomatic: (Auspicious Rites VI)

sentences.zh: ○皇太子冠禮皇子附公主笄禮公主下降儀宗室附親王納妃品官婚禮士庶人婚禮

translations.literal: ○ Crown Prince Capping Ceremony; Imperial Sons Marrying; Princess Hairpin Ceremony; Princess Leaving the Palace Ceremony; Imperial Clan Marrying; Imperial Princes Taking Consorts; Ranked Officials' Wedding Ceremony; Commoners' Wedding Ceremony
translations.idiomatic: ○ Crown prince capping; imperial sons' marriages; princess hairpin rite; princess leaving the palace; imperial clansmen's marriages; imperial princes taking consorts; ranked officials' weddings; commoners' weddings

sentences.zh: 皇太子冠儀，嚐行於大中祥符之八年。

translations.literal: The crown prince capping ceremony had once been performed in the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince capping rite had been carried out once before, in the eighth year of the Dazhong Xiangfu reign (1015).

sentences.zh: 徽宗親製《冠禮沿革》十一卷，命儀禮局仿以編次。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong personally composed eleven fascicles of "Evolution of Capping Rites," ordering the Bureau of Ceremonial to compile and arrange [the ceremony] according to it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong personally compiled eleven fascicles entitled Evolution of Capping Rites and instructed the Bureau of Ceremonial to organize the ritual according to that model.

sentences.zh: 其儀：前期奏告天地、宗廟、神稷、諸陵、宮觀。

translations.literal: The ceremony: in the preliminary period, memorial reports were submitted to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, the spirit of the altars of soil and grain, the various imperial tombs, and the palace abbeys.
translations.idiomatic: The procedure was as follows. In advance, memorials were presented to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, all imperial mausoleums, and the palace Daoist establishments.

sentences.zh: 殿中監帥尚舍張設垂拱、文德殿門之內，設香案殿下螭陛間，又為房於東朵殿。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace Secretariat led the Masters of Lodging to set up [the hall] inside the gates of the Chui-gong and Wende Palaces; incense tables were set between the laced dragons on the stairway before the hall platform; and a chamber was also made in the eastern side-hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Palace Secretariat directed the Masters of Lodging to arrange the interiors of the Chuihong and Wende palace gates, placed incense tables on the dragon-figured steps below the hall platform, and prepared a side room in the eastern auxiliary hall.

sentences.zh: 大晟展宮架樂於橫街南，太常設 太子冠席東階上、東宮官位於後，設褥位，陳服於席南，東領北上。

translations.literal: The Dasheng Office deployed the palace frame music south of the cross street; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set the crown prince's capping seat on the eastern steps, with Eastern Palace officials' positions behind it; a cushioned seat was set out, and garments were displayed south of the seat, aligned east-leading north-up.
translations.idiomatic: The Dasheng Music Office set up the palace frame orchestra south of the cross street. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices placed the crown prince's capping seat on the eastern steps, with positions for Eastern Palace officials behind it, a cushioned seat, and ceremonial dress laid out to the south of the seat, facing east with the leading edge to the north.

sentences.zh: 遠遊冠簪導、袞冕簪導同箱，在服南。

translations.literal: The cap-pin guides for the Cap of Distant Travels and for the imperial robe-and-cap were in the same box, south of the garments.
translations.idiomatic: The hairpin guides for the Cap of Distant Travels and for the imperial robe-and-crown were kept in the same case, placed south of the dress.

sentences.zh: 設罍洗阼階東，罍在洗東，篚在洗西，實巾一，加勺冪。

translations.literal: A jar and wash-basin were set east of the eastern steps of the main hall; the jar was east of the basin, the basket west of the basin, with one towel placed inside, and a ladle and cover added.
translations.idiomatic: A wine jar and wash basin were placed to the east of the eastern steps of the main hall: the jar to the east of the basin, a basket to the west, one towel inside, and a ladle with its cover set on top.

sentences.zh: 光祿設醴席西階上，南面，實側尊在席南。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Commissariat set the ceremonial wine seat on the western steps, facing south, with a side vessel filled and placed south of the seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Commissariat arranged the ceremonial wine seat on the western steps, facing south, with a filled side vessel placed to its south.

sentences.zh: 又設饌於席，加冪。

translations.literal: Food was also set on the seat, with a cover added.
translations.idiomatic: Food offerings were also laid on the seat and covered.

sentences.zh: 執事者並公服，立罍洗酒饌之所。

translations.literal: All attendants wore official dress and stood at the places of the jar, wash-basin, wine, and food.
translations.idiomatic: All attendants wore official robes and stood at their stations by the jar, wash basin, wine, and food.

sentences.zh: 九旒冕、遠遊冠、折上巾各一匴，奉禮郎三人執以侍於東階之東、 西北上。

translations.literal: One box each for the nine-tassel crown, the Cap of Distant Travels, and the folded-up kerchief; three Masters of Ceremonial held them in attendance east of the eastern steps, aligned northwest-leading north-up.
translations.idiomatic: One case each held the nine-tassel crown, the Cap of Distant Travels, and the folded kerchief; three Masters of Ceremonial bore them in attendance to the east of the eastern steps, aligned toward the northwest with the leading edge to the north.

sentences.zh: 設典儀位於宮架東北，讚者二人在南，西向。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies' position was set northeast of the palace frame; two announcers were to the south, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies took his place northeast of the palace frame orchestra, while two announcers stood to the south, facing west.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、通事舍人、太常博士引太子詣朵殿東房。

translations.literal: Ritual officers, Communication Chamber attendants, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians led the crown prince to the eastern chamber of the side hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers, Communication Chamber attendants, and academicians of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices escorted the crown prince to the eastern room of the side hall.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乘輦，駐垂拱殿，百官起居如月朔視朝 儀。

translations.literal: The emperor rode the palanquin and halted at the Chui-gong Palace; the hundred officials paid their respects as in the first-day-of-the-month audience ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode in the imperial palanquin and stopped at the Chuihong Palace, while the officials performed the salutations prescribed for the first-day audience of the month.

sentences.zh: 左輔版奏中嚴，內外符寶郎奉寶先出；

translations.literal: The Left Assistant reported on the board that the inner vigil had begun; the inner and outer seal-and-talisman officers presented the seals and went out first;
translations.idiomatic: The Left Assistant reported from the memorial board that the inner vigil had begun, and the inner and outer seal officers brought out the imperial seals first;

sentences.zh: 左輔奏外辦，皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍詣文德殿，簾卷。

translations.literal: The Left Assistant reported that the outer preparations were complete; the emperor donned the Piercing Heaven crown and crimson gauze robe and proceeded to the Wende Palace; the curtains were raised.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Assistant reported that the outer preparations were complete. The emperor put on the Piercing Heaven crown and crimson gauze robe and went to the Wende Palace as the curtains were raised.

sentences.zh: 大樂正令撞黃鍾之鍾，右五鍾皆應。

translations.literal: The Director of Great Music ordered the yellow bell struck; the five bells to the right all responded.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Great Music had the yellow bell struck, and the five bells to its right all chimed in response.

sentences.zh: 殿上鳴鞭，皇帝出西閣乘輦， 協律郎俯伏，跪，舉麾，興，工鼓，奏《乾安之樂》，殿上扇合。

translations.literal: A whip was sounded in the hall; the emperor came out of the western pavilion and mounted the palanquin; the pitch-regulation officer prostrated himself, knelt, raised the baton, rose, the musicians drummed, and "Qian'an" music was performed; the fans in the hall were closed.
translations.idiomatic: A whip cracked in the hall. The emperor emerged from the western pavilion and mounted the palanquin. The pitch officer prostrated himself, knelt, raised his baton, and rose as the musicians struck up; the piece Qian'an was played, and the hall fans were folded shut.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、太常博士引禮儀使導皇帝出，降輦即坐，簾卷扇開，鞭鳴樂止，爐煙升。

translations.literal: Ritual officers and Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians led the master of rites to guide the emperor out; he descended from the palanquin and took his seat; the curtains were raised and fans opened; the whip sounded and music ceased; censer smoke rose.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers and academicians of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices led the master of ceremonies to escort the emperor out. He stepped down from the palanquin and took his seat; the curtains were raised and the fans opened; at the crack of the whip the music stopped and incense smoke rose from the braziers.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎奉寶陳於 御坐左右，禮直官、通事舍人、太常博士引掌冠、讚冠者入門，《肅安之樂》作，至位，樂止。

translations.literal: Seal officers presented the seals and set them to the left and right of the imperial seat; ritual officers, Communication Chamber attendants, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians led the crown-placers and crown-praisers through the gate; "Su'an" music was performed; when they reached their positions, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Seal officers brought forward the imperial seals and placed them on either side of the throne. Ritual officers, Communication Chamber attendants, and academicians escorted the crown-placers and crown-praisers through the gate to the music of Su'an; when they reached their stations, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 典儀曰“再拜”，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies said, "Double bow," and all those in position double-bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies called for a double bow, and everyone in attendance performed it.

sentences.zh: 左輔詣御坐前，承製降東階，詣掌 冠者前西向稱有制，典儀讚在位官再拜訖，宣製曰：“皇太子冠，命卿等行禮。

translations.literal: The Left Assistant went before the imperial seat, received the edict, descended the eastern steps, went before the crown-placers, faced west, and announced that there was an edict; the master of ceremonies had the officials in position double-bow; then the edict was proclaimed: "The crown prince is to be capped; I command you to perform the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Assistant approached the throne, received the edict, descended the eastern steps, and stood west-facing before the crown-placers to announce that an edict was forthcoming. After the master of ceremonies had the officials in attendance perform a double bow, the edict was read: "The crown prince is to receive his cap; I command you to conduct the ceremony.

sentences.zh: ”掌冠、讚冠者再拜訖，文臣侍從官、宗室、武臣節度使以上升殿，東西立，應行禮 官詣東階下立。

translations.literal: " The crown-placers and crown-praisers finished double-bowing; civil attendant officials, imperial clansmen, and military officials of regional commissioner rank and above ascended the hall and stood east and west; officials who were to perform the ceremony went to stand below the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown-placers and crown-praisers completed their double bows. Civil attendant officials, imperial clansmen, and military commissioners and above ascended the hall and took their places to east and west, while the officials who were to take part in the rite stood below the eastern steps.

sentences.zh: 東宮官入，詣太子東房，次禮直官等引太子，內侍二人夾侍，東宮官後從，《欽安之樂》作，即席西向坐，樂止。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace officials entered and went to the crown prince's eastern chamber; next ritual officers and others led the crown prince, with two inner attendants attending on either side and Eastern Palace officials following behind; "Qin'an" music was performed; he took his seat facing west; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Palace officials entered and went to the crown prince's eastern room. Ritual officers then escorted the crown prince out, flanked by two inner attendants with Eastern Palace officials following behind, to the music of Qin'an. He took his seat facing west, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 引掌冠、讚冠者以次 詣罍洗，樂作，搢笏，盥帨訖，出笏，升，樂止。

translations.literal: The crown-placers and crown-praisers were led in turn to the jar and wash-basin; music was performed; they inserted their tablets, washed and dried their hands, finished, withdrew their tablets, ascended, and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-placers and crown-praisers were led in succession to the wash basin. Music played as they inserted their tablets, washed and dried their hands, withdrew their tablets, and ascended; then the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 執折上巾者升，掌冠者降一等受之，右執項，左執前，進皇太子席前，北向立，祝曰：“谘爾元子，肇冠於阼。

translations.literal: The bearer of the folded-up kerchief ascended; the crown-placer descended one step to receive it, holding the nape with his right hand and the front with his left, advanced before the crown prince's seat, stood facing north, and offered the blessing: "I announce to you, eldest son, that you are first capped at the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant bearing the folded kerchief ascended. The crown-placer stepped down one level to receive it, grasping the rear with his right hand and the front with his left, and advanced to stand north-facing before the crown prince's seat. He pronounced the blessing: "I announce to you, eldest son, that you are first capped at the eastern steps.

sentences.zh: 筮 日擇賓，德成禮具。

translations.literal: The day was divined and the guest chosen; virtue was complete and the rites were ready.
translations.idiomatic: The auspicious day was chosen by divination and the ceremonial guest selected; virtue was fulfilled and the rites made complete.

sentences.zh: 於萬斯年，承天之祜。

translations.literal: For ten thousand years may you receive Heaven's blessing."
translations.idiomatic: For ten thousand years may you receive Heaven's blessing."

sentences.zh: ”乃跪冠，《順安之樂》作，掌冠者興，）〉

translations.literal: " He then knelt to place the cap; "Shun'an" music was performed; the crown-placer rose.)
translations.idiomatic: He then knelt to set the cap on his head as Shun'an was played; the crown-placer rose.)

sentences.zh: 席南北面立，

translations.literal: He stood north-facing before the seat,
translations.idiomatic: He stood facing north before the seat,

translations.literal: (Hereafter follow this pattern.)
translations.idiomatic: (The same applies hereafter.)

sentences.zh: 讚冠者進席前，北面跪正冠，興，立於掌冠者之 後。

translations.literal: The crown-praiser advanced before the seat, knelt facing north to straighten the cap, rose, and stood behind the crown-placer.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-praiser stepped forward before the seat, knelt north-facing to adjust the cap, rose, and took his place behind the crown-placer.

sentences.zh: 太子興，內侍跪進服，服訖，樂止。

translations.literal: The crown prince rose; inner attendants knelt to present the garments; when he was dressed, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince rose while inner attendants knelt to bring forward his garments. Once he was dressed, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 掌冠者揖太子復坐，禮直官等引掌冠者降詣罍洗，如上儀。

translations.literal: The crown-placer bowed to the crown prince to return to his seat; ritual officers and others led the crown-placer down to the jar and wash-basin, as in the preceding ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-placer gestured for the crown prince to resume his seat, and ritual officers escorted him down to the wash basin as before.

sentences.zh: 讚冠者進席前，北向跪，脫折上巾置於匴，興，內 侍跪受，興，置於席。

translations.literal: The crown-praiser advanced before the seat, knelt facing north, removed the folded-up kerchief and placed it in the box, rose; inner attendants knelt to receive it, rose, and placed it on the seat.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-praiser advanced before the seat, knelt north-facing, removed the folded kerchief and placed it in the case, then rose. Inner attendants knelt to receive it, rose, and set it on the seat.

sentences.zh: 執遠遊冠者升，掌冠者降二等受之，右執項，左執前，進太子席前，北向立，祝曰：“爰即令辰，申加元服。

translations.literal: The bearer of the Cap of Distant Travels ascended; the crown-placer descended two steps to receive it, holding the nape with his right hand and the front with his left, advanced before the crown prince's seat, stood facing north, and offered the blessing: "On this auspicious hour we add the second cap.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant bearing the Cap of Distant Travels ascended. The crown-placer stepped down two levels to receive it, grasping the rear with his right hand and the front with his left, and advanced to stand north-facing before the crown prince's seat. He pronounced the blessing: "On this auspicious hour we confer the second cap.

sentences.zh: 崇學以讓，三善皆得。

translations.literal: Honor learning through yielding; the three excellences are all attained.
translations.idiomatic: Revere learning through humility; the three virtues of the Eastern Palace are all fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 副予一 人，受天百福。

translations.literal: Assist me, the One Man; receive Heaven's hundred blessings."
translations.idiomatic: Stand as my second self; receive Heaven's hundred blessings."

sentences.zh: ”乃跪冠，《懿安》之樂作，掌冠者興。

translations.literal: " He then knelt to place the cap; "Yi'an" music was performed; the crown-placer rose.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt to set the cap as Yi'an was played, and the crown-placer rose.

sentences.zh: 讚冠者進，跪簪結紘，興。

translations.literal: The crown-praiser advanced, knelt to pin and tie the cap-strings, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-praiser stepped forward, knelt to insert the hairpin and tie the cap strings, and rose.

sentences.zh: 太子興，內侍跪進服，服訖，樂止。

translations.literal: The crown prince rose; inner attendants knelt to present the garments; when he was dressed, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince rose while inner attendants knelt to bring forward his garments. Once he was dressed, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 掌冠者揖太子復坐，掌冠者降 詣罍洗，及讚冠者跪，脫遠遊冠，並如上儀。

translations.literal: The crown-placer bowed to the crown prince to return to his seat; the crown-placer descended to the jar and wash-basin, and the crown-praiser knelt and removed the Cap of Distant Travels—all as in the preceding ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-placer gestured for the crown prince to resume his seat, then went down to the wash basin while the crown-praiser knelt to remove the Cap of Distant Travels, all as before.

sentences.zh: 執袞冕者升，掌冠者降三等受之，右執項，左執前，進太子席前，北向立，祝曰：“三加彌尊，國本以正。

translations.literal: The bearer of the imperial robe-and-cap ascended; the crown-placer descended three steps to receive it, holding the nape with his right hand and the front with his left, advanced before the crown prince's seat, stood facing north, and offered the blessing: "With the third addition ever more honored, the foundation of the state is made right.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant bearing the imperial robe-and-crown ascended. The crown-placer stepped down three levels to receive it and advanced to stand north-facing before the crown prince's seat. He pronounced the blessing: "With the third investiture ever more exalted, the foundation of the realm is secured.

sentences.zh: 無疆惟休， 有室大競。

translations.literal: Boundless blessings alone; the house has great strength.
translations.idiomatic: May your blessings know no bounds; may your house grow ever mighty.

sentences.zh: 懋昭厥德，保茲永命。

translations.literal: Greatly display your virtue; preserve this everlasting mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Greatly manifest your virtue and preserve this everlasting mandate."

sentences.zh: ”乃跪冠，《成安之樂》作。

translations.literal: " He then knelt to place the cap; "Cheng'an" music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt to set the cap as Cheng'an was played.

sentences.zh: 掌冠者興。

translations.literal: The crown-placer rose.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-placer rose.

sentences.zh: 讚冠者如上儀，跪簪結紘。

translations.literal: The crown-praiser, as in the preceding ceremony, knelt to pin and tie the cap-strings.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-praiser, as before, knelt to insert the hairpin and tie the cap strings.

sentences.zh: 內侍進服，服訖，樂止。

translations.literal: Inner attendants presented the garments; when he was dressed, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants brought forward his garments; once he was dressed, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 禮直官等引太子降自東階，樂作，由 西階升，即醴席南向坐，樂止。

translations.literal: Ritual officers and others led the crown prince down the eastern steps; music was performed; he ascended by the western steps and took his seat facing south at the ceremonial wine seat; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers escorted the crown prince down the eastern steps to music, then up the western steps to take his seat facing south at the ceremonial wine seat; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 又引掌冠者詣罍洗，樂作，盥帨訖，升西階，樂止。

translations.literal: They again led the crown-placer to the jar and wash-basin; music was performed; he washed and dried his hands, finished, ascended the western steps, and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They again led the crown-placer to the wash basin. Music played as he washed and dried his hands, then ascended the western steps; the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 讚冠者跪取爵，內侍注酒，掌冠者受爵，跪進太子席前，北向立，祝曰：“旨酒 嘉薦，有飶其香。

translations.literal: The crown-praiser knelt to take the goblet; inner attendants poured the wine; the crown-placer received the goblet, knelt and advanced before the crown prince's seat, stood facing north, and offered the blessing: "Fine wine, excellent offering, richly fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-praiser knelt to take the goblet while inner attendants poured the wine. The crown-placer received it, knelt, and advanced to stand north-facing before the crown prince's seat. He pronounced the blessing: "Fine wine, a worthy offering, richly fragrant.

sentences.zh: 拜受祭之，以定爾祥。

translations.literal: Bow, receive, and offer it in sacrifice to secure your good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Bow, receive it, and offer it in sacrifice to secure your good fortune.

sentences.zh: 令德壽豈，日進無疆。

translations.literal: With excellent virtue, long life, and joy; may you advance daily without limit."
translations.idiomatic: With excellent virtue, long life, and joy; may you advance daily without limit."

sentences.zh: ”太子搢圭，跪受爵，《正安之樂》作，飲訖，奠爵執圭。

translations.literal: " The crown prince inserted his tablet, knelt to receive the goblet; "Zheng'an" music was performed; when he had drunk, he set down the goblet and held the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince inserted his tablet and knelt to receive the goblet as Zheng'an was played. When he had drunk, he set down the goblet and took up his tablet.

sentences.zh: 太官令設饌席前，太子搢圭，食訖，樂 止，執圭興，太官令徹饌、爵。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Kitchen set food before the seat; the crown prince inserted his tablet, ate, and finished; the music ceased; he held the tablet and rose; the Director of the Imperial Kitchen removed the food and goblet.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Kitchen set food before the seat. The crown prince inserted his tablet and ate; when he had finished, the music stopped. He rose holding his tablet, and the Director removed the food and goblet.

sentences.zh: 禮直官等引自西階詣東房，易朝服，降立橫街，南北向，東宮官復位，西向。

translations.literal: Ritual officers and others led [him] from the western steps to the eastern chamber to change into court dress, descended and stood on the cross street facing south, and Eastern Palace officials returned to their positions facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers escorted him from the western steps to the eastern room to change into court dress, then led him down to stand on the cross street facing south, while Eastern Palace officials returned to their stations facing west.

sentences.zh: 〈（太子初行，樂作，至位，樂止。）〉

translations.literal: (When the crown prince first set out, music was performed; when he reached his position, the music ceased.)
translations.idiomatic: (When the crown prince first set out, music played; when he reached his station, it stopped.)

sentences.zh: 禮直 官等引掌冠、讚冠者詣前，西向，掌冠者少進，字之曰：“始生而名，為實之賓。

translations.literal: Ritual officers and others led the crown-placers and crown-praisers forward, facing west; the crown-placer advanced slightly and bestowed the style-name, saying: "At birth one is given a personal name, as a guest of substance.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers escorted the crown-placers and crown-praisers forward to face west. The crown-placer stepped slightly ahead and bestowed the style-name, saying: "At birth one receives a personal name, as a guest among the living.

sentences.zh: 既冠而字，以益厥文。

translations.literal: Once capped one receives a style-name, to augment one's refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Once capped one receives a style-name, to augment one's cultivation.

sentences.zh: 永受保之，承天之慶。

translations.literal: May you forever receive its protection and inherit Heaven's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: May you forever be guarded by it and receive Heaven's blessing.

sentences.zh: 奉敕字某。

translations.literal: By imperial command, the style-name is [X].
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command, your style-name is [X].

sentences.zh: ”太常博士請再拜，太子 再拜訖，搢笏，舞蹈，再拜，奏聖躬萬福，又再拜。

translations.literal: " A Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician requested a double bow; the crown prince finished double-bowing, inserted his tablet, performed the dance-bow, double-bowed again, reported that the sacred person enjoyed ten thousand blessings, and double-bowed once more.
translations.idiomatic: " An academician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices called for a double bow. The crown prince completed it, inserted his tablet, performed the dance-bow and another double bow, reported that the Son of Heaven enjoyed ten thousand blessings, and bowed again.

sentences.zh: 左輔承旨，降自東階，詣太子前，西向，宣曰“有敕”，太子再拜，宣敕曰：“事親以孝，接下以仁。

translations.literal: The Left Assistant received the command, descended the eastern steps, went before the crown prince, faced west, and announced, "There is an edict"; the crown prince double-bowed; the edict was proclaimed: "Serve your parents with filial piety; treat your subordinates with benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Assistant received the command, descended the eastern steps, and stood west-facing before the crown prince to announce, "There is an edict." The crown prince double-bowed, and the edict was read: "Serve your parents with filial piety; treat your subordinates with benevolence.

sentences.zh: 遠佞近 義，祿賢使能。

translations.literal: Keep flatterers at a distance and draw the righteous near; reward the worthy and employ the capable.
translations.idiomatic: Keep sycophants at a distance and draw the righteous near; reward the worthy and employ the capable.

sentences.zh: 古訓是式，大猷是經。

translations.literal: Take ancient teachings as your model; make the great plan your constant guide."
translations.idiomatic: Take the teachings of antiquity as your model; make the great design your constant guide."

sentences.zh: ”宣訖，太子再拜訖，禮直官等引太子前，俯伏，跪，奏稱：“臣雖不敏，敢不祗奉！

translations.literal: " When the proclamation was finished, the crown prince finished double-bowing; ritual officers and others led the crown prince forward; he prostrated himself, knelt, and reported: "Though your servant is not clever, how dare he not reverently obey!"
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation ended, the crown prince completed his double bow. Ritual officers led him forward; he prostrated himself, knelt, and reported: "Though your servant is not clever, how dare he fail to obey reverently!

sentences.zh: ”奏訖，興，復位，再拜訖，引出殿 門，樂作，出門，樂止。

translations.literal: " When the report was finished, he rose, returned to his position, finished double-bowing, and was led out through the hall gate; music was performed; when he had gone out, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished, he rose, returned to his place, completed his double bow, and was escorted out through the hall gate to music; once he had left, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 侍立官並降復位，典儀曰“拜”，讚者承傳，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: All attending officials also descended and returned to their positions; the master of ceremonies said, "Bow," the announcers transmitted it, and all those in position double-bowed.
translations.idiomatic: All attending officials descended and returned to their stations. The master of ceremonies called for a bow; the announcers relayed the command, and everyone in attendance performed a double bow.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏禮畢，鳴鞭。

translations.literal: The master of rites reported that the ceremony was complete; a whip was sounded.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies reported that the rite was complete, and a whip was cracked.

sentences.zh: 大樂正令撞蕤賓之鍾，左五鍾皆應，《乾安之樂》作， 皇帝降坐，左輔奏解嚴，放仗，在位官皆再拜，退。

translations.literal: The Director of Great Music ordered the rui-bin bell struck; the five bells to the left all responded; "Qian'an" music was performed; the emperor descended from his seat; the Left Assistant reported that the vigil was ended and the guard relieved; all officials in position double-bowed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Great Music had the rui-bin bell struck, and the five bells to its left chimed in response as Qian'an was played. The emperor rose from his seat; the Left Assistant reported that the vigil was ended and the guard stood down; all officials in attendance performed a double bow and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太子入內，朝見皇后，如宮中儀。

translations.literal: The crown prince entered the inner quarters and paid his respects to the empress, as in the palace ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince entered the inner palace and paid his respects to the empress according to the palace rites.

sentences.zh: 乃擇日謁太廟、別廟，宿齋於本宮。

translations.literal: Then a day was chosen to visit the Grand Ancestral Temple and the separate temples; he fasted and purified himself overnight in his own palace.
translations.idiomatic: A day was then chosen to visit the Grand Ancestral Temple and the subsidiary temples, and he kept an overnight fast in his own palace.

sentences.zh: 質明，服遠遊冠、朱明衣，乘金輅。

translations.literal: At dawn he donned the Cap of Distant Travels and vermilion-bright robes and rode the golden chariot.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he put on the Cap of Distant Travels and vermilion ceremonial robes and rode in the golden imperial chariot.

sentences.zh: 至廟，改服袞冕，執圭行禮，群臣稱賀，皇帝賜酒三行。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the temple, he changed into the imperial robe-and-cap, held the tablet, and performed the rites; the hundred officials offered congratulations; the emperor bestowed wine in three rounds.
translations.idiomatic: At the temple he changed into the imperial robe-and-crown, performed the rites holding his tablet, received congratulations from the officials, and was granted three rounds of wine by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 皇子冠，前期擇日奏告景靈宮，太常設皇子冠席文德殿東階上，稍北東向，設褥席，陳服於席南，東領北上。

translations.literal: Imperial sons' capping: in the preliminary period a day was chosen and a memorial report submitted to the Jingling Palace; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set the imperial sons' capping seat on the eastern steps of the Wende Palace, slightly to the north and facing east; a cushioned seat was set out; garments were displayed south of the seat, aligned east-leading north-up.
translations.idiomatic: For the capping of imperial sons, a day was chosen in advance and a memorial presented to the Jingling Palace. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices placed the capping seat on the eastern steps of the Wende Palace, slightly to the north and facing east, with a cushioned seat and ceremonial dress laid out to its south, aligned east with the leading edge to the north.

sentences.zh: 九旒冕服、七梁進賢冠服、折上巾公服、七梁冠簪導、九旒冕簪導同箱，在服南。

translations.literal: The nine-tassel crown dress, seven-ribbed worthy's cap dress, folded-up kerchief official dress, seven-ribbed cap hairpin guide, and nine-tassel crown hairpin guide were in the same box, south of the garments.
translations.idiomatic: The nine-tassel crown ensemble, seven-ribbed worthy's cap ensemble, folded kerchief official dress, and the hairpin guides for the seven-ribbed cap and nine-tassel crown were kept in the same case south of the dress.

sentences.zh: 設罍洗、酒饌、旒冕、冠、巾及執事者，並如皇太子儀。

translations.literal: The setting out of the jar, wash-basin, wine, food, tasseled crown, caps, kerchief, and attendants—all followed the crown prince ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The wine jar, wash basin, wine, food, tasseled crown, caps, kerchief, and attendants were all arranged as in the crown prince ceremony.

sentences.zh: 其日質明，皇帝通天冠、絳紗袍，禦文德殿。

translations.literal: On that day at dawn the emperor wore the Piercing Heaven crown and crimson gauze robe and held court in the Wende Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On that day at dawn the emperor wore the Piercing Heaven crown and crimson gauze robe and took his place in the Wende Palace.

sentences.zh: 皇子自東房出，內侍二人夾侍，王府官從，《恭安之樂》作，即席南向坐，樂止。

translations.literal: The imperial son came out from the eastern chamber, with two inner attendants attending on either side and princely establishment officials following; "Gong'an" music was performed; he took his seat facing south; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial son emerged from the eastern room, flanked by two inner attendants with officials of his princely establishment following behind, to the music of Gong'an. He took his seat facing south, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 掌冠者進折上巾，北向跪冠，《修 安之樂》作；

translations.literal: The crown-placer advanced with the folded-up kerchief, knelt facing north to place the cap; "Xiu'an" music was performed;
translations.idiomatic: The crown-placer advanced with the folded kerchief and knelt north-facing to set the cap as Xiu'an was played;

sentences.zh: 讚冠者進，北面跪正冠，皇子興，內侍跪進服訖，樂止。

translations.literal: the crown-praiser advanced, knelt facing north to straighten the cap; the imperial son rose; inner attendants knelt to present the garments; when he was dressed, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: the crown-praiser stepped forward and knelt north-facing to adjust the cap. The imperial son rose while inner attendants knelt to bring forward his garments; once he was dressed, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 掌冠者揖皇子復坐，以爵跪進，祝曰：“酒醴和旨，籩豆靜嘉。

translations.literal: The crown-placer bowed to the imperial son to return to his seat, knelt with the goblet and advanced, offering the blessing: "The wine and sweet brew are harmonious and fine; the platters and stands are pure and excellent.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-placer gestured for the imperial son to resume his seat, then knelt with the goblet and advanced to pronounce the blessing: "The wine and sweet brew are harmonious and fine; the platters and stands are pure and excellent.

sentences.zh: 授爾元服，兄弟具來。

translations.literal: We confer upon you the first cap; brothers all have come.
translations.idiomatic: We confer upon you your first cap; your brothers have all gathered.

sentences.zh: 永言保 之，降福孔皆。

translations.literal: May you forever guard it; may blessings descend upon you in full measure."
translations.idiomatic: May you forever guard it; may blessings descend upon you in full measure."

sentences.zh: ”皇子搢笏，跪受爵，《翼安之樂》作，飲訖，太官令進饌訖。

translations.literal: " The imperial son inserted his tablet, knelt to receive the goblet; "Yi'an" music was performed; when he had drunk, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen advanced the food and finished.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial son inserted his tablet and knelt to receive the goblet as Yi'an was played. When he had drunk, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen brought forward the food.

sentences.zh: 再加七梁冠，《進安之樂》作。

translations.literal: The second addition was the seven-ribbed cap; "Jin'an" music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: For the second investiture he received the seven-ribbed cap as Jin'an was played.

sentences.zh: 掌冠者進爵，祝曰：“賓讚既戒，殽核惟旅。

translations.literal: The crown-placer advanced with the goblet and offered the blessing: "The guest and praiser have both been warned; the meats and fruits are all set out.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-placer advanced with the goblet and pronounced the blessing: "The guest and praiser have both been admonished; the meats and fruits are all laid out.

sentences.zh: 申加厥 服，禮儀有序。

translations.literal: We add the second cap; the rites and ceremonies are in proper order.
translations.idiomatic: We confer the second cap; the rites proceed in proper order.

sentences.zh: 允觀爾成，承天之祜。

translations.literal: May we behold your completion; receive Heaven's blessing."
translations.idiomatic: May we behold your fulfillment; receive Heaven's blessing."

sentences.zh: ”皇子跪受爵，《輔安之樂》作，太官奉饌。

translations.literal: " The imperial son knelt to receive the goblet; "Fu'an" music was performed; the Director of the Imperial Kitchen presented the food.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial son knelt to receive the goblet as Fu'an was played, and the Director of the Imperial Kitchen presented the food.

sentences.zh: 三加九旒冕，《廣安之樂》作。

translations.literal: The third addition was the nine-tassel crown; "Guang'an" music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: For the third investiture he received the nine-tassel crown as Guang'an was played.

sentences.zh: 掌冠者進爵，祝曰：“旨酒嘉栗，甘薦令芳。

translations.literal: The crown-placer advanced with the goblet and offered the blessing: "Fine wine and excellent grain; sweet offerings, fragrant and fine.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-placer advanced with the goblet and pronounced the blessing: "Fine wine and excellent grain; sweet offerings, fragrant and fine.

sentences.zh: 三 加爾服，眉壽無疆。

translations.literal: With the third addition to your dress, may your eyebrows reach old age without limit."
translations.idiomatic: With the third investiture of your dress, may you enjoy boundless longevity."

sentences.zh: 永承天休，俾熾而昌。

translations.literal: May you forever receive Heaven's favor; may you flourish and prosper."
translations.idiomatic: May you forever receive Heaven's grace; may you flourish and thrive.

sentences.zh: ”皇子跪受爵，《賢安》之樂作，太官奉饌，饌徹。

translations.literal: " The imperial son knelt to receive the goblet; the music 《Xian'an》 was performed; the Director of the Imperial Kitchen presented the food; the food was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial son knelt to receive the goblet as 《Xian'an》 was played. The Director of the Imperial Kitchen presented the food, and when the meal was finished it was cleared away.

sentences.zh: 皇子降，易朝服，立橫階南，北向位，掌冠者字之 曰：“歲日雲吉，威儀孔時。

translations.literal: The imperial son descended, changed into court dress, and stood south of the cross step in a north-facing position; the crown-placer bestowed his style name, saying: "The year and day are auspicious; the bearing and rites are perfectly timed.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial son descended, changed into court dress, and took his place south of the cross step, facing north. The crown-placer bestowed his style name, saying: "The year and day are auspicious; your bearing and rites are perfectly timed.

sentences.zh: 昭告厥字，君子攸宜。

translations.literal: We clearly announce your style name; fitting for a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: We clearly announce your style name, as befits a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 順爾成德，永受保之。

translations.literal: Follow your accomplished virtue; may you forever be protected in receiving it.
translations.idiomatic: Follow your mature virtue; may you forever be protected.

sentences.zh: 奉敕字某。

translations.literal: By imperial command, the style-name is [X].
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command, the style-name is [X].

sentences.zh: ”皇子再拜舞蹈，又再拜，奏聖躬萬福，又再拜。

translations.literal: " The imperial son performed double bows with ceremonial dance, bowed again, reported a wish for the sovereign's ten thousand blessings, and bowed again.
translations.idiomatic: " The imperial son bowed twice with ceremonial dance, bowed again, wished the sovereign ten thousand blessings, and bowed once more.

sentences.zh: 左輔宣敕，戒曰：“好禮樂 善，服儒講藝。

translations.literal: The Left Assistant proclaimed the edict, admonishing: "Love ritual, music, and goodness; serve Confucian learning and cultivate the arts.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Assistant proclaimed the edict and admonished: "Love ritual, music, and goodness; devote yourself to Confucian learning and the arts.

sentences.zh: 蕃我王室，友於兄弟。

translations.literal: Make flourish our royal house; be friendly with your brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Make our royal house flourish; be a true friend to your brothers.

sentences.zh: 不溢不驕，惟以守之。

translations.literal: Neither overflowing nor arrogant—only thus guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Neither excessive nor arrogant—guard these precepts always.

sentences.zh: ”皇子再拜，進前俯伏，跪稱：“臣雖不敏，敢不祗奉！

translations.literal: " The imperial son bowed twice, advanced, prostrated himself, and kneeling said: "Though I am unworthy, how dare I not reverently obey!
translations.idiomatic: " The imperial son bowed twice, advanced, prostrated himself, and kneeling said: "Though I am unworthy, how dare I not obey reverently!

sentences.zh: ”俯伏，興，復位，再拜，出。

translations.literal: " He prostrated himself, rose, returned to his place, bowed twice, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " He prostrated himself, rose, returned to his place, bowed twice, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 殿上侍立官並 降，復位，再拜，放仗。

translations.literal: All attendants standing in the hall also descended, returned to their places, bowed twice, and the guard staves were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: All attendants standing in the hall likewise descended, returned to their places, bowed twice, and the guard staves were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 明日，百僚詣東上閣門賀。

translations.literal: The next day, the hundred officials went to the Eastern Upper Gate of the Communication Chamber to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, all officials went to the Eastern Upper Gate of the Communication Chamber to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 公主笄禮。

translations.literal: The princess hairpin ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The princess hairpin ceremony.

sentences.zh: 年十五，雖未議下嫁，亦笄。

translations.literal: At age fifteen, even if marriage had not yet been discussed, the hairpin rite was still performed.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen, even if no marriage had yet been arranged, the hairpin rite was still performed.

sentences.zh: 笄之日，設香案於殿庭；

translations.literal: On the day of the hairpin ceremony, an incense table was set in the hall courtyard;
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the ceremony, an incense table was placed in the hall courtyard;

sentences.zh: 設冠席於東房外，坐東向西；

translations.literal: a capping seat was placed outside the eastern room, seated facing east toward the west;
translations.idiomatic: a capping seat was set up outside the eastern room, facing east toward the west;

sentences.zh: 設 醴席於西階上，坐西向東；

translations.literal: a ceremonial wine seat was placed on the western steps, seated facing west toward the east;
translations.idiomatic: a ceremonial wine seat was placed on the western steps, facing west toward the east;

sentences.zh: 設席位於冠席南，西向。

translations.literal: a seat was placed south of the capping seat, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: and a seat was placed south of the capping seat, facing west.

sentences.zh: 其裙背、大袖長裙、褕翟之衣，各設於椸，陳下庭；

translations.literal: The skirt-back, wide-sleeved long skirt, and feathered ceremonial robes were each placed on clothes racks and displayed in the lower courtyard;
translations.idiomatic: The skirt-back, wide-sleeved long skirt, and feathered ceremonial robes were each hung on racks and displayed in the lower courtyard;

sentences.zh: 冠笄、冠朵、九翬四鳳冠，各置於盤，蒙以帕。

translations.literal: The hairpin cap, cap ornament, and nine-plume four-phoenix crown were each placed on trays and covered with cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The hairpin cap, cap ornament, and nine-plume four-phoenix crown were each placed on trays and covered with cloth.

sentences.zh: 首飾隨之， 陳於服椸之南，執事者三人掌之。

translations.literal: Head ornaments followed, displayed south of the garment racks; three attendants were in charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: Head ornaments followed and were displayed south of the garment racks; three attendants were put in charge of them.

sentences.zh: 櫛總置於東房。

translations.literal: Comb and hair bindings were placed in the eastern room.
translations.idiomatic: Comb and hair bindings were placed in the eastern room.

sentences.zh: 內執事宮嬪盛服旁立，俟樂作，奏請皇帝升御坐，樂止。

translations.literal: Inner-attendant palace ladies in full dress stood by; when the music began they reported requesting the emperor to ascend the imperial throne; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Palace ladies serving as inner attendants, dressed in full ceremonial garb, stood by. When the music began they reported requesting the emperor to ascend the throne; the music then stopped.

sentences.zh: 提舉官奏曰：“公主行笄禮。

translations.literal: The supervising officer reported: "The princess is performing the hairpin ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising officer reported: "The princess is performing the hairpin ceremony.

sentences.zh: ”樂作，讚者 引公主入東房。

translations.literal: " Music played; the announcer led the princess into the eastern room.
translations.idiomatic: " Music played, and the announcer led the princess into the eastern room.

sentences.zh: 次行尊者為之總髻畢，出，即席西向坐。

translations.literal: Next an elder of rank bound her hair into a bun; when finished she came out and took her seat facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Next an elder of rank bound her hair into a bun. When that was done she came out and took her seat facing west.

sentences.zh: 次引掌冠者東房，西向立，執事奉冠笄以進，掌冠者進前一步受之，進公主席前，北向立，樂止，祝曰：“ 令月吉日，始加元服。

translations.literal: Next the crown-placer was led to the eastern room and stood facing west. Attendants presented the hairpin cap; the crown-placer advanced one step to receive it, then advanced before the princess's seat and stood facing north. The music stopped, and he offered the blessing: "On this auspicious month and day, you first receive the cap and dress.
translations.idiomatic: Next the crown-placer was led to the eastern room and stood facing west. Attendants brought forward the hairpin cap; the crown-placer advanced one step to receive it, then moved before the princess's seat and stood facing north. When the music stopped, he pronounced the blessing: "On this auspicious month and day, you first receive your cap and dress.

sentences.zh: 棄爾幼誌，順爾成德。

translations.literal: Put aside your childhood ways; follow your mature virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Put aside your childhood ways; follow your mature virtue.

sentences.zh: 壽考綿鴻，以介景福。

translations.literal: Long life without end; may great blessings attend you.
translations.idiomatic: May you live long without end and receive great blessings.

sentences.zh: ”祝畢，樂作，東向冠之，冠畢，席南北向立；

translations.literal: " When the blessing was finished, music played; he capped her facing east; when the capping was done, he stood north-facing before the seat;
translations.idiomatic: " When the blessing was finished, music played. He placed the cap on her facing east; when the capping was done, he stood north-facing before the seat;

sentences.zh: 讚冠者為之正冠，施首飾畢，揖公主適房，樂 止。

translations.literal: the crown-praiser straightened the cap for her; when the head ornaments were applied, he gestured for the princess to go to her room; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: the crown-praiser straightened her cap and applied the head ornaments. When that was done, he gestured for the princess to go to her room, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 執事者奉裙背入，服畢，樂作，公主就醴席，掌冠者揖公主坐。

translations.literal: Attendants brought in the skirt-back; when she was dressed, music played; the princess went to the wine seat, and the crown-placer gestured for her to sit.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants brought in the skirt-back. When she was dressed, music played; the princess went to the wine seat, and the crown-placer gestured for her to sit.

sentences.zh: 讚冠者執酒器，執事者酌酒，授於掌冠者執酒，北向立，樂止，祝曰：“酒醴和旨，籩豆靜嘉。

translations.literal: The crown-praiser held the wine vessel; attendants poured wine and handed it to the crown-placer, who stood facing north. The music stopped, and he offered the blessing: "The wine and sweet brew are harmonious and fine; the platters and stands are pure and excellent.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-praiser held the wine vessel while attendants poured wine and handed it to the crown-placer, who stood facing north. When the music stopped, he pronounced the blessing: "The wine and sweet brew are harmonious and fine; the platters and stands are pure and excellent.

sentences.zh: 受爾元服，兄弟具來。

translations.literal: Receive your first cap; brothers have all come.
translations.idiomatic: Receive your first cap; your brothers have all gathered.

sentences.zh: 與國同休，降福孔皆。

translations.literal: Share the realm's repose; may blessings descend in full measure.
translations.idiomatic: Share the realm's peace; may blessings descend upon you in full measure.

sentences.zh: ”祝畢，樂作，進酒，公主飲畢，讚冠者受酒器，執事者奉饌，食訖，徹饌。

translations.literal: " When the blessing was finished, music played; wine was brought forward; when the princess had drunk, the crown-praiser received the vessel; attendants presented food; when she had eaten, the food was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: " When the blessing was finished, music played. Wine was brought forward; when the princess had drunk, the crown-praiser received the vessel. Attendants presented food, and when she had eaten, the food was cleared away.

sentences.zh: 復引公主至冠席坐，樂止。

translations.literal: The princess was led back to the capping seat to sit; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was led back to the capping seat to sit, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 讚冠者至席前，讚冠者脫冠置於槃，執事者徹去，樂作。

translations.literal: The crown-praiser came before the seat, removed the cap and placed it on a tray; attendants withdrew it; music played.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-praiser came before the seat, removed the cap and placed it on a tray, and attendants withdrew it as music played.

sentences.zh: 執事者奉冠以進，掌冠者進前二步受之，進公主席前，北向立，樂止，祝曰：“吉月令辰，乃申爾服，飾以 威儀，淑謹爾德。

translations.literal: Attendants presented the cap; the crown-placer advanced two steps to receive it, advanced before the princess's seat and stood facing north. The music stopped, and he offered the blessing: "On this auspicious month and appointed time, we add to your dress; adorn yourself with dignified bearing; be virtuous and careful in your conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants brought forward the cap; the crown-placer advanced two steps to receive it, then moved before the princess's seat and stood facing north. When the music stopped, he pronounced the blessing: "On this auspicious month and appointed time, we add to your dress; adorn yourself with dignified bearing; be virtuous and careful in your conduct.

sentences.zh: 眉壽永年，享受遐福。

translations.literal: May your eyebrows reach old age for endless years; enjoy far-reaching blessings.
translations.idiomatic: May you enjoy endless years and far-reaching blessings.

sentences.zh: ”祝畢，樂作，東向冠之，冠畢，席南北向立。

translations.literal: " When the blessing was finished, music played; he capped her facing east; when done, he stood north-facing before the seat.
translations.idiomatic: " When the blessing was finished, music played. He placed the cap on her facing east, and when that was done he stood north-facing before the seat.

sentences.zh: 讚冠者為之正冠，施首飾畢，揖公主適房，樂止。

translations.literal: The crown-praiser straightened the cap and applied the head ornaments; when finished he gestured for the princess to go to her room; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-praiser straightened her cap and applied the head ornaments. When that was done, he gestured for the princess to go to her room, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 執事奉大袖長裙入，服 畢，樂作。

translations.literal: Attendants brought in the wide-sleeved long skirt; when she was dressed, music played.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants brought in the wide-sleeved long skirt. When she was dressed, music played.

sentences.zh: 公主至醴席，掌冠者揖公主坐。

translations.literal: The princess went to the wine seat; the crown-placer gestured for her to sit.
translations.idiomatic: The princess went to the wine seat, and the crown-placer gestured for her to sit.

sentences.zh: 讚冠者執酒器，執事者酌酒，授於掌冠者執酒，北向立，樂止，祝曰：“賓讚既戒，肴核惟旅。

translations.literal: The crown-praiser held the wine vessel; attendants poured wine and handed it to the crown-placer, who stood facing north. The music stopped, and he offered the blessing: "The guest and praiser have both been admonished; the meats and fruits are all laid out.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-praiser held the wine vessel while attendants poured wine and handed it to the crown-placer, who stood facing north. When the music stopped, he pronounced the blessing: "The guest and praiser have both been admonished; the meats and fruits are all laid out.

sentences.zh: 申加爾服，禮儀有序。

translations.literal: We add to your dress; the rites and ceremonies are in proper order.
translations.idiomatic: We confer the second cap; the rites proceed in proper order.

sentences.zh: 允 觀爾成，永天之祜。

translations.literal: May we behold your fulfillment; receive Heaven's lasting blessing.
translations.idiomatic: May we behold your fulfillment; receive Heaven's lasting blessing.

sentences.zh: ”祝畢，樂作，進酒，公主飲畢，讚冠者受酒器，執事者奉饌食訖，徹饌。

translations.literal: " When the blessing was finished, music played; wine was brought forward; when the princess had drunk, the crown-praiser received the vessel; attendants presented food; when she had eaten, the food was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: " When the blessing was finished, music played. Wine was brought forward; when the princess had drunk, the crown-praiser received the vessel. Attendants presented food, and when she had eaten, the food was cleared away.

sentences.zh: 復引公主至冠席坐，樂作。

translations.literal: The princess was led back to the capping seat to sit; music played.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was led back to the capping seat to sit as music played.

sentences.zh: 讚冠者至席前，讚冠者脫冠 置於盤，執事者徹去，樂作。

translations.literal: The crown-praiser came before the seat, removed the cap and placed it on a tray; attendants withdrew it; music played.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-praiser came before the seat, removed the cap and placed it on a tray, and attendants withdrew it as music played.

sentences.zh: 執事奉九翬四鳳冠以進，掌冠者進前三步受之，進公主席前，向北而立，樂止，祝曰：“以歲之吉，以月之令，三加爾服，保茲永命。

translations.literal: Attendants presented the nine-plume four-phoenix crown; the crown-placer advanced three steps to receive it, advanced before the princess's seat and stood facing north. The music stopped, and he offered the blessing: "With the year's auspiciousness and the month's proper season, with the third addition to your dress, preserve this eternal mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants brought forward the nine-plume four-phoenix crown; the crown-placer advanced three steps to receive it, then moved before the princess's seat and stood facing north. When the music stopped, he pronounced the blessing: "With the year's auspiciousness and the month's proper season, with the third addition to your dress, preserve this eternal mandate.

sentences.zh: 以終厥德，受天之慶。

translations.literal: Complete your virtue; receive Heaven's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Complete your virtue and receive Heaven's blessing.

sentences.zh: ”祝畢，樂作，東向冠之，冠畢，席南北向立。

translations.literal: " When the blessing was finished, music played; he capped her facing east; when done, he stood north-facing before the seat.
translations.idiomatic: " When the blessing was finished, music played. He placed the cap on her facing east, and when that was done he stood north-facing before the seat.

sentences.zh: 讚冠者為之正冠、施首飾畢，揖公主適房，樂止。

translations.literal: The crown-praiser straightened the cap and applied the head ornaments; when finished he gestured for the princess to go to her room; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-praiser straightened her cap and applied the head ornaments. When that was done, he gestured for the princess to go to her room, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 執事者奉褕翟之衣入，服畢，樂作，公主至 醴席，掌冠者揖公主坐。

translations.literal: Attendants brought in the feathered ceremonial robes; when she was dressed, music played; the princess went to the wine seat; the crown-placer gestured for her to sit.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants brought in the feathered ceremonial robes. When she was dressed, music played; the princess went to the wine seat, and the crown-placer gestured for her to sit.

sentences.zh: 讚冠者執酒器，執事者酌酒，授於掌冠者執酒，北向立，樂止，祝曰：“旨酒嘉薦，有飶其香。

translations.literal: The crown-praiser held the wine vessel; attendants poured wine and handed it to the crown-placer, who stood facing north. The music stopped, and he offered the blessing: "Fine wine, excellent offerings, richly fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: The crown-praiser held the wine vessel while attendants poured wine and handed it to the crown-placer, who stood facing north. When the music stopped, he pronounced the blessing: "Fine wine and excellent offerings, richly fragrant.

sentences.zh: 鹹加爾服，眉壽無疆。

translations.literal: With the third addition to your dress, may your eyebrows reach old age without limit."
translations.idiomatic: With the third investiture of your dress, may you enjoy boundless longevity."

sentences.zh: 永承天休，俾熾而 昌。

translations.literal: May you forever receive Heaven's favor; may you flourish and prosper.
translations.idiomatic: May you forever receive Heaven's grace; may you flourish and thrive.

sentences.zh: ”祝畢，樂作，進酒，公主飲畢，讚冠者受酒器。

translations.literal: " When the blessing was finished, music played; wine was brought forward; when the princess had drunk, the crown-praiser received the vessel.
translations.idiomatic: When the blessing was finished, music played. Wine was brought forward; when the princess had drunk, the crown-praiser received the vessel.

sentences.zh: 執事者奉饌，食訖，徹饌。

translations.literal: Attendants presented food; when she had eaten, the food was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants presented food, and when she had eaten, the food was cleared away.

sentences.zh: 復引公主至席位立，樂止，掌冠者詣前相對，致辭曰：“歲日具吉， 威儀孔時。

translations.literal: The princess was led back to her seat to stand; the music stopped; the crown-placer came forward to face her and delivered the address: "The year and day are fully auspicious; the bearing and rites are perfectly timed.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was led back to her seat to stand, and the music stopped. The crown-placer came forward to face her and delivered the address: "The year and day are fully auspicious; your bearing and rites are perfectly timed.

sentences.zh: 昭告厥字，令德攸宜。

translations.literal: We clearly announce your style name; your excellent virtue is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: We clearly announce your style name, as your excellent virtue requires.

sentences.zh: 表爾淑美，永保受之。

translations.literal: Display your graceful beauty; may you forever be protected in receiving it.
translations.idiomatic: Display your graceful beauty; may you forever be protected.

sentences.zh: 可字曰某。

translations.literal: Your style-name shall be [X].
translations.idiomatic: Your style-name shall be [X].

sentences.zh: ”辭訖，樂作，掌冠者退。

translations.literal: " When the address was finished, music played; the crown-placer withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " When the address was finished, music played and the crown-placer withdrew.

sentences.zh: 引公主至君父之前，樂止，再拜起居，謝恩再拜。

translations.literal: The princess was led before her sovereign father; the music stopped; she bowed twice and reported her well-being, then bowed twice in thanks for the grace.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was led before her sovereign father. When the music stopped, she bowed twice and reported her well-being, then bowed twice again in thanks for the imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 少俟，提舉進御坐 前承旨訖，公主再拜。

translations.literal: After a brief wait, the supervising officer advanced before the imperial throne and received the decree; when finished, the princess bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: After a brief wait, the supervising officer advanced before the imperial throne and received the decree. When that was done, the princess bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 提舉乃宣訓辭曰：“事親以孝，接下以慈。

translations.literal: The supervising officer then proclaimed the instructional address: "Serve your parents with filial piety; treat those below you with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising officer then proclaimed the instructional address: "Serve your parents with filial piety; treat those below you with kindness.

sentences.zh: 和柔正順，恭儉謙儀。

translations.literal: Be gentle, compliant, upright, and obedient; be respectful, frugal, and modest in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Be gentle, compliant, upright, and obedient; be respectful, frugal, and modest in bearing.

sentences.zh: 不溢不驕，毋詖毋欺。

translations.literal: Neither overflowing nor arrogant; neither slander nor deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Neither excessive nor arrogant; neither slander nor deceit.

sentences.zh: 古訓是式，爾其守之。

translations.literal: Take the ancient precepts as your model; guard them well.
translations.idiomatic: Take the ancient precepts as your model and guard them well.

sentences.zh: ”宣訖，公主再拜，前奏 曰：“兒雖不敏，敢不祗承！

translations.literal: " When the proclamation was finished, the princess bowed twice, advanced and reported: "Though I am unworthy, how dare I not reverently accept!
translations.idiomatic: " When the proclamation was finished, the princess bowed twice, advanced, and reported: "Though I am unworthy, how dare I not accept reverently!

sentences.zh: ”歸位再拜，見後母之禮如之。

translations.literal: " She returned to her place and bowed twice; the rites for greeting the empress were the same.
translations.idiomatic: " She returned to her place and bowed twice. The rites for greeting the empress were performed in the same way.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，公主復坐，皇后稱賀，次妃嬪稱賀，次掌冠、讚冠者謝恩，次提舉眾內臣稱賀，其餘班次稱賀，並依常式。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, the princess resumed her seat; the empress offered congratulations, then the consorts and concubines, then the crown-placer and crown-praiser thanked for the grace, then the supervising officer and all inner attendants offered congratulations; the remaining ranks offered congratulations—all according to usual form.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete, the princess resumed her seat. The empress offered congratulations, then the consorts and concubines, then the crown-placer and crown-praiser thanked the court for the grace, then the supervising officer and all inner attendants offered congratulations. The remaining ranks offered congratulations as well—all according to usual form.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，樂作；

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, music played;
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete, music played;

sentences.zh: 駕興，樂止。

translations.literal: the imperial palanquin was raised; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: the imperial palanquin was raised, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 公主下降。

translations.literal: Princess marriage (leaving the palace for marriage).
translations.idiomatic: Princess marriage.

sentences.zh: 初被選尚者即拜駙馬都尉，賜玉帶、襲衣、銀鞍勒馬、采羅百匹，謂之係親。

translations.literal: As soon as a man was chosen to marry in, he was appointed Commandant Escort of the Heir Apparent and granted a jade belt, ceremonial robe, silver saddle and bridled horse, and a hundred bolts of colored silk—this was called tying the kinship bond.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as a man was chosen to marry a princess, he was appointed Commandant Escort of the Heir Apparent and granted a jade belt, ceremonial robe, silver saddle and bridled horse, and a hundred bolts of colored silk. This was called tying the kinship bond.

sentences.zh: 又賜辦財銀萬兩，進財之數，倍於親王聘禮。

translations.literal: Wedding preparation funds of ten thousand taels of silver were also granted; the quantity of marriage gifts was double that of an imperial prince's betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Wedding preparation funds of ten thousand taels of silver were also granted, and the quantity of marriage gifts was double that of an imperial prince's betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 出降，賜甲第。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the palace in marriage, a finest-tier mansion was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Upon leaving the palace in marriage, a finest-tier mansion was granted.

sentences.zh: 餘如諸王夫 人之製。

translations.literal: The rest followed the regulations for imperial princes' consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed the regulations for imperial princes' consorts.

sentences.zh: 掌扇加四，引障花、燭籠各加十，皆行舅姑之禮。

translations.literal: Four ceremonial fans were added; ten each of flower screens and candle lanterns were added; all performed the rites toward parents-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Four ceremonial fans were added, along with ten each of flower screens and candle lanterns, and all performed the rites toward parents-in-law.

sentences.zh: 諸親遞加賜賚。

translations.literal: Relatives by marriage received additional gifts in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives by marriage received additional gifts in succession.

sentences.zh: 其縣主係親以金帶，賜辦財銀五千兩，納財賜賚，大率三分減其二。

translations.literal: For county princesses, the kinship bond used a gold belt; wedding preparation funds of five thousand taels of silver were granted; marriage gifts and rewards were generally reduced by two-thirds.
translations.idiomatic: For county princesses, the kinship bond used a gold belt and wedding preparation funds of five thousand taels of silver were granted; marriage gifts and rewards were generally reduced by two-thirds.

sentences.zh: 宗室女特封郡君者， 又差降焉。

translations.literal: For clanswomen specially enfeoffed as Ladies of a Commandery, the benefits were further reduced.
translations.idiomatic: For clanswomen specially enfeoffed as Ladies of a Commandery, the benefits were reduced still further.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐初，禮官言：“禮閣新儀，公主出降前一日，行五禮。

translations.literal: In the early Jiayou era, ritual officials said: "According to the new ritual code in the Ceremonial Archive, one day before a princess left the palace in marriage, the five marriage rites were performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jiayou era, ritual officials said: "According to the new ritual code in the Ceremonial Archive, one day before a princess left the palace in marriage, the five marriage rites were performed.

sentences.zh: 古者，結婚始用行人，告以夫家采擇之意，謂之納采。

translations.literal: In antiquity, marriage began by sending emissaries to inform the bride's family of the groom's family's intention to select a match—this was called presenting the initial gift.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, marriage began when emissaries were sent to inform the bride's family of the groom's family's intention to select a match. This was called presenting the initial gift.

sentences.zh: 問女之名，歸卜夫廟， 吉，以告女家，謂之問名、納吉。

translations.literal: The bride's name was asked; divination was performed at the groom's ancestral temple; if auspicious, the bride's family was informed—this was called asking the name and presenting the auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: The bride's name was asked, divination was performed at the groom's ancestral temple, and if the result was auspicious the bride's family was informed. This was called asking the name and presenting the auspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 今選尚一出朝廷，不待納采。

translations.literal: Now the selection and marriage assignment come solely from the court, without waiting for presenting the initial gift.
translations.idiomatic: Now the selection and marriage assignment come solely from the court, without waiting for the initial gift.

sentences.zh: 公主封爵已行誕告，不待問名。

translations.literal: The princess's enfeoffment and rank announcement had already been promulgated, without waiting to ask the name.
translations.idiomatic: The princess's enfeoffment and rank announcement had already been promulgated, without waiting to ask her name.

sentences.zh: 若納成則既有進財，請期則有司擇日。

translations.literal: For presenting the marriage gift, marriage gifts were already brought; for setting the date, the relevant offices chose the day.
translations.idiomatic: For presenting the marriage gift, marriage gifts were already brought; for setting the date, the relevant offices chose the day.

sentences.zh: 宜稍依五禮之名，存其物數， 俾知婚姻之事重、而夫婦之際嚴如此，亦不忘古禮之義也。

translations.literal: It would be appropriate to follow somewhat the names of the five rites and preserve their ritual objects and quantities, so that people would know marriage is weighty and the relationship between husband and wife is solemn as this—and so the meaning of the ancient rites would not be forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: It would be appropriate to follow somewhat the names of the five rites and preserve their ritual objects and quantities, so that people would know how weighty marriage is and how solemn the bond between husband and wife ought to be—and so the meaning of the ancient rites would not be forgotten.

sentences.zh: ”時兗國公主下嫁李瑋，詔賜出降日，令夫家主婚者具合用雁、幣、玉、馬等物，陳於內東門外，以授內 謁者，進入內侍掌事者受，唯馬不入。

translations.literal: " At that time when the Princess of Yan'guo married Li Wei, an edict fixed the day of her departure from the palace and ordered the groom's family, represented by the officiating host, to prepare the requisite wild geese, silks, jade, horses, and other items, display them outside the Inner Eastern Gate, and present them to the inner ushers, who would deliver them to the chief inner attendant to receive—only the horses did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time, when the Princess of Yan'guo married Li Wei, an edict fixed the day of her departure from the palace and ordered the groom's family, represented by the officiating host, to prepare the requisite wild geese, silks, jade, horses, and other items, display them outside the Inner Eastern Gate, and present them to the inner ushers to be delivered to the chief inner attendant. Only the horses did not enter.

sentences.zh: 康國公主下降，太常寺言：“按令，公主出降，申中書省，請皇后帥宮闈掌事人送至第外，命婦從，今請如令。

translations.literal: When the Princess of Kangguo left the palace in marriage, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "According to regulations, when a princess left the palace in marriage, memorial was submitted to the Secretariat; the empress was requested to lead palace attendants to escort her to outside the mansion, with lady companions following—we now request to follow the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Princess of Kangguo left the palace in marriage, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "According to regulations, when a princess left the palace in marriage, memorial was submitted to the Secretariat and the empress was requested to lead palace attendants to escort her to outside the mansion, with lady companions following. We now request to follow the regulations.

sentences.zh: ”詔：“出降日，婉儀帥宮闈掌事者送至第外，命婦免從。”

translations.literal: " An edict responded: "On the day of departure from the palace, a Lady of Handsome Fairness shall lead palace attendants to escort her to outside the mansion; lady companions are exempt from following.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict responded: "On the day of departure from the palace, a Lady of Handsome Fairness shall lead palace attendants to escort her to outside the mansion; lady companions are exempt from following.

sentences.zh: 徽宗改公主為姬，下詔曰：“在熙寧初，有詔厘改公主、郡主、縣主名稱，當時群臣不克奉承。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong changed the title princess to ji (king's daughter), and issued an edict saying: "In the early Xining era, there was an edict to reform the titles of princess, commandery princess, and county princess, but the ministers at the time could not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong changed the title princess to ji and issued an edict saying: "In the early Xining era, there was an edict to reform the titles of princess, commandery princess, and county princess, but the ministers at the time could not carry it out.

sentences.zh: 近命有司稽考前世，周稱‘王姬’，見於《詩•雅》。

translations.literal: Recently I ordered the relevant offices to examine former ages; the Zhou called them 'Wang Ji' (king's daughters), as seen in the Greater Odes section of the 《Book of Songs》.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I ordered the relevant offices to examine former ages. The Zhou called them 'king's daughters,' as seen in the Greater Odes section of the 《Book of Songs》.

sentences.zh: ‘姬’雖周 姓，考古立製，宜莫如周。

translations.literal: Although 'ji' is a Zhou surname, when examining antiquity to establish institutions, none is as fitting as the Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Although ji is a Zhou surname, when we examine antiquity to establish institutions, none is as fitting as the Zhou model.

sentences.zh: 可改公主為帝姬、郡主為宗姬、縣主為族姬。

translations.literal: The title princess may be changed to emperor's daughter (di ji), commandery princess to lineage daughter (zong ji), and county princess to clan daughter (zu ji).
translations.idiomatic: Princess may be renamed emperor's daughter, commandery princess renamed lineage daughter, and county princess renamed clan daughter.

sentences.zh: 其稱大長者，為大長帝姬，仍以美名二字易其國號，內兩國者以四字。”

translations.literal: Those styled grand-elder were styled grand-elder emperor's daughter; the two-character elegant name still replaced their state title, and those with two states within used four characters.
translations.idiomatic: Those styled grand-elder became grand-elder emperor's daughters; the two-character elegant name still replaced their state title, and those bearing two state names used four characters.

sentences.zh: 其出降日，婿家具五禮，修表如上儀。

translations.literal: On the day of her departure from the palace, the groom's family prepared the five rites and drew up a memorial according to the ritual above.
translations.idiomatic: On the day she left the palace in marriage, the groom's family prepared the five rites and drew up a memorial according to the ritual above.

sentences.zh: 太史局擇日告廟。

translations.literal: The Astrological Bureau chose a day and notified the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Astrological Bureau chose an auspicious day and notified the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 親迎。

translations.literal: Personally welcoming the bride.
translations.idiomatic: Personally welcoming the bride.

sentences.zh: 前一日，所司於內東門外量地之宜，西向設婿次。

translations.literal: On the day before, the relevant offices measured suitable ground outside the Inner Eastern Gate and set up the groom's pavilion facing west.
translations.idiomatic: On the day before, the relevant offices measured suitable ground outside the Inner Eastern Gate and set up the groom's pavilion facing west.

sentences.zh: 其日，婿父醮子如上儀。

translations.literal: On that day, the groom's father performed the libation-capping for his son according to the ritual above.
translations.idiomatic: On that day, the groom's father performed the libation for his son according to the ritual above.

sentences.zh: 乃命之曰：“往迎肅雍，以昭惠宗祏。

translations.literal: He then charged him, saying: "Go to welcome her with solemn grace, to manifest favor to the ancestral temple tablets.
translations.idiomatic: He then charged him, saying: "Go to welcome her with solemn grace, to show favor to the ancestral tablets.

sentences.zh: ”子再拜，曰：“祗率嚴命！

translations.literal: " The son bowed twice and said: "I respectfully accept your stern charge!
translations.idiomatic: " The son bowed twice and said: "I respectfully accept your solemn charge!

sentences.zh: ”又再拜， 降，出乘馬，至東華門內下馬，禮直官引就次。

translations.literal: " He bowed twice again, descended, went out and mounted a horse; upon reaching inside the Eastern Flowery Gate he dismounted, and the ritual officer led him to the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: " He bowed twice again, descended, went out and mounted a horse. Upon reaching inside the Eastern Flowery Gate he dismounted, and the ritual officer led him to the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 有司陳帝姬鹵簿、儀仗於內東門外，候將升厭翟車，引婿出次於內東門外，躬身西向。

translations.literal: The relevant offices displayed the emperor's daughter's guard of honor and ritual insignia outside the Inner Eastern Gate; when she was about to ascend the black-lacquered pheasant carriage, they led the groom out from the pavilion to outside the Inner Eastern Gate, where he bowed his body facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices displayed the emperor's daughter's guard of honor and ceremonial insignia outside the Inner Eastern Gate. When she was about to ascend the black-lacquered pheasant carriage, they led the groom out from the pavilion to outside the Inner Eastern Gate, where he bowed facing west.

sentences.zh: 掌事者執雁，內謁者奉雁以 進，俟帝姬升車，婿再拜，先還第。

translations.literal: The chief attendant held the wild goose; the inner usher presented the goose and advanced; when the emperor's daughter had mounted the carriage, the groom bowed twice and returned first to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The chief attendant held the wild goose; the inner usher presented it and advanced. When the emperor's daughter had mounted the carriage, the groom bowed twice and returned first to his residence.

sentences.zh: 同牢。

translations.literal: Sharing the sacrificial pen.
translations.idiomatic: Sharing the sacrificial feast.

sentences.zh: 其日初昏，掌事者設巾、洗各二於東階東南，一於室北。

translations.literal: At early dusk that day, the chief attendant set out two cloths and two basins each at the southeast of the eastern steps, and one at the north of the chamber.
translations.idiomatic: At early dusk that day, the chief attendant set out two cloths and two basins at the southeast of the eastern steps, and one at the north of the chamber.

sentences.zh: 水在洗東，尊於室中，實四爵、兩巹於篚。

translations.literal: Water was placed east of the basin; a wine vessel was placed in the chamber; four cups and two nuptial cups were filled in the basket.
translations.idiomatic: Water was placed east of the basin, a wine vessel in the chamber, and four cups and two nuptial cups filled in the basket.

sentences.zh: 婿至本第，下馬以俟。

translations.literal: The groom arrived at his residence, dismounted, and waited.
translations.idiomatic: The groom arrived at his residence, dismounted, and waited.

sentences.zh: 帝姬至，降車，讚者引婿揖之以入，及寢門又揖，導之升階，入室盥洗。

translations.literal: When the emperor's daughter arrived, she descended from the carriage; the announcer led the groom to bow to her and enter; at the bedroom gate he bowed again, and guided him up the steps to enter the chamber and wash hands and face.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's daughter arrived, she descended from the carriage. The announcer led the groom to bow to her and enter; at the bedroom gate he bowed again and guided him up the steps to enter the chamber and wash.

sentences.zh: 掌事者布對位，又揖帝姬，皆即坐受盞三飲，俱興，再拜，讚者徹酒。
